title: Opus 5 procedural shoreline with voxel sea life.  Very chill to watch :)
author: octaviustf
selftext: Really impressed with Opus 5 - using artifacts and code to build out and incorporate different features. Any thoughts on what to add next?

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: Voxel is getting a lot nicer. Hopefully we will reach the point where people saying just because its voxel its a Minecraft clone(even though Minecraft is NOT the first voxel game,just the most popular)

replies.author: Muted-Koala1325
replies.body: True, Minecraft started out as an Infiniminer clone, not many people know that and they call stuff a Minecraft clone 🙄

comments.author: No_Toe_7069
comments.body: Are all the voxel animals generated by Opus? that shark looks great

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Yes I use artifacts to create the voxel creatures with animations just first then import into project

replies.author: DrEndGame
replies.body:
Can you explain the workflow in a bit more detail? New trying to learn. 

When you say artifact, are you saying you built that using Claude artifacts? What was the prompt? Any other frameworks you used or you just asked it to use voxels?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: hi yes- i use claude artifacts for smaller more scoped tasks like creating the voxel shark (it can create a tweakable generator to modify/and dial in) then i export the html to Claude Code to incorporate into the project.  My prompt is something like "detailed animated procedural voxel shark/turtle,etc."

replies.author: CyDenied
replies.body: so you're having claude.ai make it, and you give that url to claude code CLI?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: I paste the code generated from the Artifacts into Claude Code - hope that helps

comments.author: DrEndGame
comments.body: As for suggestions - would love to see if you could get kelp to work. Especially have your shark swim through that and have the kelp be pushed aside as it's swimming through.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: great idea! I'll work on that and getting a demo up

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body: Love the lighting and the smoothness

comments.author: procgen
comments.body: Love this. Reminds me of those fish tank screensavers that were popular in the 90s/early 2000s.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: ya that was part of my inspiration!

comments.author: fnwc
comments.body: have Claude make it into a screensaver

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: that's great idea!

replies.author: fnwc
replies.body: Other than different sea creatures - crabs, octopi, shellfish, jellyfish, incandescent algae, starfish, etc. - day/night cycles, rain.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Incandescent with night cycle would be fun - great idea

comments.author: ideaofsoul
comments.body: How you creating this quality? i cant get this realistic games. what you use?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Thanks! I use Claude artifacts for the specific voxel creatures and then Claude Code 5 - on Max setting

comments.author: Keltharious
comments.body: What's your prompt? I have a few ideas for this style of sandbox. Looks super fun!

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: i started withe something like "top down shallow water scene with voxel shark in 3js" and took a fair amount of iteration to get the visuals correct. I started using Claude on Max instead of High and noticed a quality difference (a good one) in my opinion.

replies.author: Keltharious
replies.body: I had this idea for a 14th century peasant walking through a town square. I might adapt it with your prompt; it could be fun assuming it does things proportionally correct.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: ya i've found voxel modeling to be pretty reliable if you like the look- takes some iteration- you could try using artifacts to dial in the peasant as well as the procedural buildings and then bring the files into Code to create the experience- also try using artifacts for the torch

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: It's really cool but a bit sparse for my tastes.  Would be awesome to see a dense, lush, coral reef with tons more stuff.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Thanks- working on adding more life :)

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: Beautiful job! This is how it's done!

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Thanks!

comments.author: thepaulbooth
comments.body: Wow this is one of the most impressive ones I've seen. The water effects and little fish behavior are so good.

replies.author: Muted-Koala1325
replies.body: Agreed!

comments.author: OkEntertainment2154
comments.body: This is oddly relaxing to watch 😄. I'd love to see some weather effects next,maybe waves during a storm or a day/night cycle with bioluminescent sea life.

comments.author: Muted-Koala1325
comments.body: Would love to see your Voxel animations creator artifact, is it public?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: I will put up the whole project in a public repo over next few days

comments.author: GamingLimsha
comments.body: That is smooth animation and model. Is this all made from Opus or you are using some other tools too?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Just Opus

comments.author: Caitlin_Shaw
comments.body: love the bubbling bgm! almost like asmr

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Thanks I’m going to add some more procedural music and may some other SFX as well.

comments.author: justaguy3252
comments.body: This looks really good, what is your goal with this game?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Thanks! honestly just kind of creating a chill screen to watch while I'm at the office lol - I did end up making it multiplayer because I get lonely during the day and would be cool if some other sharks joined the reef ;).

replies.author: justaguy3252
replies.body:
Nice, now you're giving me an idea for my office slack.

What would be cool is having your shark grow up in some way, maybe through feeding it or having it explore the reef and feeding on things there.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Ya starting with baby shark and having it feed and grow would be cool!
